title: Split Bruhat affine stratification over arbitrary fields
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $H$ a reductive $F$-group [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]: smooth affine of finite type, geometrically connected, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup after algebraic closure. Let $T\subseteq B\subseteq H$, where $T$ is a split maximal torus [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type] and $B$ is a split solvable Borel subgroup [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure, def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors]. Here a Borel is a smooth connected closed subgroup maximal among smooth connected solvable closed subgroups, and split solvable means a finite series of smooth connected closed subgroups normal in their predecessor with quotients $\mathbf G_a$ or $\mathbf G_m$. Let $Q=H/B$ be the scheme representing the fppf sheafification of $A\mapsto H(A)/B(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented covers. Then $Q$ is smooth projective geometrically integral over $F$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-projective-morphism, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. It has a finite stratification $Q=\coprod_{a\in I}C_a$ by locally closed subschemes $C_a\simeq\mathbf A_F^{n_a}$, $n_a\geq0$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. A stratification here is a disjoint partition of the underlying space by these locally closed subschemes. There is a distinguished index $a_0$ for which $C_{a_0}$ is open dense in $Q$ [def-weil-open-immersion]; its closure is all of $Q$, and no other stratum has this property. For every field extension $L/F$ [def-pc-field-extension], the canonical identification $Q_L=H_L/B_L$ carries the scalar extensions $C_{a,L}$ to a stratification having all the preceding properties. Geometrically integral means nonempty and integral after every field extension, with integral meaning reduced and irreducible. If $H=T$, the index set is a singleton, $n_{a_0}=0$ and $Q=\operatorname{Spec}F$.

source.place: Section 21h, standing split reductive pair over an arbitrary field; Proposition 21.70 and Theorem 21.73, printed pp.446–447; Proposition 21.79, Theorem 21.80 and Remark 21.82, pp.449–450; Theorem 21.84, p.451. Smooth projectivity of the quotient is also used in Lemma 18.21 and the opening of Section 21h, via Theorem 17.9 and the homogeneous projective embedding. No closure-incidence, Picard or Cartier-divisor assertion is included.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] to $(H,B)$. It gives a separated finite-type quotient $p:H\to Q$ which is flat, surjective and finitely presented, with coset fibres on every test scheme and fpqc-local lifts. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], the coset map identifies this quotient with the given represented fppf sheaf quotient: two lifts differ by a $B$-point, and compatible local cosets glue uniquely. For the same reason after every $L/F$, the base change represents $H_L/B_L$: local sections lift along $p_L$, and equality is exactly equality modulo $B_L$. Thus this identification is canonical, rather than an identification only on rational points.

source.place: Theorem 5.28 and Definition 5.20, pp.104--105; quotient base change by its sheaf universal property.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-split-flag-rational-fixed-scheme] to keep $B$ Borel after extension to an algebraic closure $\bar F$. The quotient over $\bar F$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-proper-geometry], so $Q_{\bar F}$ is smooth and proper. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\bar F\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is surjective flat quasi-compact. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-single-fpqc-descent] to obtain smoothness and properness of $Q$. For any $L/F$, smoothness of $Q_L$ follows from [lem-pc-proper-base-change], and hence regularity from [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. The surjection $p_L$ has connected source $H_L$ by geometric connectedness of $H$, so its continuous image $Q_L$ is connected and nonempty (it contains $eB$). The surjectivity persists by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Now [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] makes $Q_L$ integral. This proves geometric integrality over every field extension, including inseparable extensions.

source.place: Theorem 17.9(a), p.354, and Section 21h opening, p.446; descent: Stacks descent.tex Tag 02L1 (lemma-descending-property-proper).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-chevalley-scheme-line-stabilizer], choose a rational representation $H\to\operatorname{GL}(E)$ and line $D\subset E$ whose scheme-theoretic stabilizer is $B$. The morphism $h\mapsto hD$ is invariant on the coset relation. Descend it along $p$ using [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to get an $H$-equivariant map $i:Q\to\mathbf P(E)$. This map is a monomorphism: locally lift any two test points to $h_1,h_2$; equality of their lines means $h_1^{-1}h_2$ stabilizes $D$, hence lies in $B$, hence their cosets agree, and equality descends. Projective space is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated]. Since $Q$ is proper, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] makes $i$ proper, and [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] makes it a closed immersion. Its finite-type source is quasi-compact, so this is projectivity in [def-pc-projective-morphism].

source.place: Theorem 4.27 and Remark 4.30, pp.94--96; Theorem 17.9 and Section 21h opening, p.446 (homogeneous projective embedding).

proof.text: Restrict $E$ to the split torus $T$. Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition] to write it as its finite sum of character spaces. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-torus-fixed-weight-schemes] to choose a cocharacter $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to T$ separating the distinct occurring characters. It gives $\mathbf P(E)^\lambda=\mathbf P(E)^T$ and, by pullback along the equivariant closed immersion $i$, $Q^\lambda=Q^T$ as schemes. By [lem-sfb-split-flag-rational-fixed-scheme] this is the finite constant scheme with points $x_w=n_wB$, $w\in I=W(F)$. These are genuine rational reduced fixed points, even over a finite or imperfect field; no claim about fixed subschemes is inferred just from rational points.

source.place: Lemma 13.51, p.274, its following application, p.275, and the paragraph before Proposition 21.70, p.446.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-rational-projective-attracting-cells] to $Q$ with this $\lambda$ and the restricted projective representation. Step 2 gives nonemptiness, smoothness and geometric connectedness, step 3 gives the equivariant projective embedding, and step 4 gives the required finite constant fixed scheme. For $w\in I$ take $C_w=Q_{x_w}^+$, represented by evaluation at $1$ of equivariant maps $\mathbf A^1\to Q$ with value $x_w$ at zero. The cited theorem gives locally closed affine spaces $C_w\simeq\mathbf A_F^{n_w}$ partitioning $|Q|$, and exactly one open dense stratum $C_{w_0}$. It also gives that no other stratum has closure $Q$. These are precisely the stratification and uniqueness assertions required here; no Schubert boundary or closure-incidence formula is used.

source.place: Proposition 21.70 and its proof by Corollary 13.49, pp.446--447; Theorem 21.73.

proof.text: For $L/F$, step 1 identifies $Q_L$ canonically with $H_L/B_L$. The scalar-extension assertion of [lem-sfb-rational-projective-attracting-cells] identifies each $(C_w)_L$ with the attracting subscheme at $x_{w,L}$. Thus the same index set and distinguished index give the finite affine stratification and unique open dense cell after any field extension, with the same affine dimensions. Step 2 already proved integrality after all extensions. Smoothness and projectivity persist: smoothness by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], and the base-changed closed embedding from step 3 gives projectivity directly. Finally if $H=T$, the inclusions force $B=H$ and the sheaf quotient is the terminal sheaf, represented by $\operatorname{Spec}F$. By [lem-sfb-split-flag-rational-fixed-scheme] $I$ is a singleton; its single cell is all of $Q=\mathbf A_F^0$.

source.place: Chapter 21 arbitrary-field standing assumptions and Proposition 21.1; Proposition 21.70, Theorem 21.80; the scalar-extended attractor functor and rank-zero case.

Integral geometry from smoothness and connectedness, for each field extension.

Step 2: smoothness and properness over F̄ come from borel-quotient-proper-geometry and descend along Spec F̄→Spec F (the smooth-descent Mathlib leaf and proper single-fpqc descent); geometric integrality over every L comes from smooth ⇒ regular, the image of the connected H_L, and regular connected ⇒ integral. Step 3: the Chevalley line stabilizer gives a descended monomorphism into P(E), which is proper over the separated P(E) and hence a closed immersion, so Q is projective. Step 4: the weight decomposition and projective-torus-fixed-weight-schemes give λ with Q^λ=Q^T, which the fixed-flag node identifies with the constant scheme W(F). Step 5: the attracting-cell node applies, and I checked every hypothesis. Step 6: base change and the H=T case. The attracting-cell node is BB over an arbitrary field with rational isolated fixed points; it keeps projectivity, which 13.47(c) needs, and generalizes lem-sfb-projective-attracting-cells, which assumes an algebraically closed field.
